title: JFK and LaGuardia are the only scalable high-pay yellow pickup zones in Q1 2026
summary: In Q1 2026 (January–March), JFK Airport ($79.66 average passenger total) and LaGuardia Airport ($69.86) are the only high-value origins with real scale — 663k combined pickups versus a $30.33 citywide mean. Stage drivers there and in adjacent East Elmhurst / South Ozone Park in the afternoon–evening. Do not chase Newark Airport or Outside-of-NYC averages (duration artifacts), and do not leave Manhattan volume for Far Rockaway–style long, low occupied-hour trips.

datasets.question: Which pickup zones deliver the highest average passenger total per trip, and do they also have enough volume and occupied-hour earnings to justify repositioning?
What are the twelve volume-qualified pickup zones with the highest average passenger total per trip?
How do per-trip totals, occupied-hour earnings, and trip volume vary by pickup hour citywide?
At which hours do the highest per-trip-value pickup zones actually pay, so drivers are not sent to the right zone at the wrong time?

widgets.title: Highest average passenger total by pickup zone
widgets.description: Twelve volume-qualified Q1 2026 origins ranked by average passenger total (USD per trip). Newark Airport and Outside of NYC lead the axis but are not dispatch targets.
widgets.accessibilityText: Horizontal bars of the 12 volume-qualified Q1 2026 yellow pickup zones with the highest average passenger total (USD per trip). Outside of NYC ($106.40) and Newark Airport ($104.59) lead but are not local dispatch markets. JFK Airport ($79.66, 412,635 trips) and LaGuardia Airport ($69.86, 250,345) are the first real repositioning targets, then East Elmhurst ($64.56).

widgets.title: Volume versus average passenger total by zone
widgets.description: Each volume-qualified zone is a point: qualifying trips versus average passenger total (USD per trip). Occupied-hour earnings are in the tooltip only.
widgets.accessibilityText: Scatter of 209 volume-qualified pickup zones: qualifying trip count on a log x-axis versus average passenger total in USD per trip on the y-axis. JFK and LaGuardia sit upper-right (high value, high volume). Newark Airport and Outside of NYC sit upper-left. Far Rockaway is mid-value with weak occupied-hour earnings in the tooltip.

widgets.title: Citywide average passenger total by pickup hour
widgets.description: Citywide average passenger total (USD per trip) by pickup hour. The peak is pre-rush, not the 18:00 volume peak.
widgets.accessibilityText: Citywide average passenger total (USD per trip) by pickup hour 0 through 23 in Q1 2026. Highest at 05:00 ($36.32) and 04:00 ($35.01); lowest at 10:00 ($28.19), 7% below the $30.33 citywide mean. Evening hours near $30-$32 carry the most trips (peak 786,766 at 18:00) but not the highest per-trip total.

widgets.title: Citywide occupied-hour earnings by pickup hour
widgets.description: Citywide occupied-hour earnings (USD per occupied hour) by pickup hour. Overnight is strongest; mid-afternoon is weakest.
widgets.accessibilityText: Citywide occupied-hour earnings (USD per occupied hour) by pickup hour 0 through 23 in Q1 2026. Peak overnight: $133.47 at 04:00 and $129.38 at 03:00. Evening 21:00-23:00 holds $118-$121. Mid-afternoon is weakest at $90.50 at 15:00, when trips last 20.3 minutes. Occupied minutes only; no wait or deadhead.

widgets.title: Average passenger total for top-value zones by pickup hour
widgets.description: Average passenger total (USD per trip) for the twelve highest-paying volume-qualified zones at each pickup hour. Stage only bright, high-trip cells.
widgets.accessibilityText: Heatmap of average passenger total (USD per trip) for the 12 highest-paying volume-qualified zones by pickup hour 0-23, ordered top to bottom by Q1-wide average. JFK is brightest at 16:00 ($89.89 on 30,719 trips) and 17:00 ($88.42). LaGuardia pays most at 07:00-08:00 ($76-$77). Newark Airport and Outside of NYC stay high every hour but are not local markets.
